A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Commute Graph Neural Networks. All 16 pages of v4 and 18 pages of v5, including their appendices, support comparison. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable, and relocated content can be matched.

before.justification: v4 reports original node-classification experiments on eight datasets, runtime measurements, and rewiring and symmetrization ablations.

after.justification: v5 reports original classification results and ablations, plus additional sensitivity, graph-density, and directed-versus-undirected results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: v4 defines DiLap as D^-1 - P and computes commute times through an auxiliary normalized matrix R. v5 replaces this with the incidence-based operator B diag({Pij}) B^T and uses its pseudoinverse in the commute-time formulas. This changes the reported computation of aggregation weights; similarity-based rewiring and directional message passing remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate node classification on Squirrel, Chameleon, Citeseer, CoraML, AM-Photo, Snap-Patents, Roman-Empire, and Arxiv-Year. Directed and symmetrized inputs were already covered in v4. The added analyses reuse these datasets; 'citepseer' becoming 'Citeseer' is a spelling correction.

E2.justification: The same 13 baselines, including DUPLEX and DirGNN, appear in v4 Table 2 and v5 Table 1. CGNNppr and CGNNsym are retained as ablation comparators. Appendix D disaggregates results for existing methods without introducing another comparator.

E3.justification: v5 adds a sensitivity grid over five depths and five hidden widths, plus a relative edge-density diagnostic. Appendix D.1 specifies undirected-only reporting for APPNP, GPRGNN, and GCNII, qualifying v4's generic better-of-directed-and-undirected protocol. This does not establish reruns. The main data splits and accuracy metric remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices D.2–D.3 add depth/width sensitivity analysis on Squirrel and CoraML and rewiring-density analysis on three datasets. Figure 3 extends the existing heterophilic label-alignment analysis to homophilic graphs, and Table 2 adds Citeseer to commute-time preservation measurements. The PPR and symmetrization ablations remain.

E5.justification: Accuracy with standard deviation over 10 runs is already stated in v4 Table 2 and retained in v5 Appendix C.1. The additional result tables use the same reporting practice. No new seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: All eight CGNN entries change: Squirrel moves from 77.61 to 77.83, Citeseer from 70.27 to 71.59, and Arxiv-Year from 66.97 to 66.16. Baseline rows remain identical, and CGNN still leads on six datasets. Ablation scores and runtimes change, while Appendix D adds extensive results. The revised method prevents interpreting these as isolated same-method performance gains.

T1.justification: The Laplacian definition and derivation are replaced, and Proposition 4.1 with Appendix A.2 adds node-equivariance and edge-invariance proofs. The fundamental-matrix lemma, hitting/commute formulas, and corresponding proof are substantially revised. Appendix A.3 assumes an operator F - ΠP that does not match the newly defined incidence-based operator.

C1.justification: The main CGNN/DiLap contributions and six-of-eight leading-performance claim remain. v5 adds introductory claims of 2.64% and 4.17% accuracy improvements on Squirrel and Citeseer. The latter does not match Table 1: CGNN's 71.59 versus the best baseline, DUPLEX's 67.60, gives a 3.99-point margin.

C2.justification: v5 explicitly identifies dense commute-matrix memory overhead as the primary limitation and proposes local computation as future work. It adds interpretations connecting preferred depth to homophily and graph-density changes to rewiring impact. The citation-network applicability caveat was already present in v4.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 newly explains directed GCN aggregation using weights 1/sqrt(di dj) and the handling of undirected baseline settings. Sensitivity ranges are also documented. Hardware, data splits, and the typical SVD rank q = 5 were already disclosed in v4; moving these details into appendices adds no new resource information.

R1.justification: v5 removes references to Lin and Gao's magnetic framelets, Fiorini et al.'s SigMaNet, and four Zhuo papers. It shortens the GraphSAGE and DUPLEX related-work discussion, while retaining DUPLEX as a baseline. The broader positioning against directed Laplacians and directed GNNs remains.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 6; pseudocode, experimental settings, and dataset statistics move into Appendices B–C. The method exposition is substantially rewritten, the conclusion is condensed, and additional experiments receive Appendix D. Author and affiliation text and several terminology errors also change.

P2.justification: v5 substantially rearranges and enlarges displays. The old bar chart labeled Table 3 becomes part of two-panel Figure 3; new sensitivity heatmaps and Tables 6–8 present additional analyses and detailed results. Statistics and pseudocode move to appendices. The runtime plots are retained and enlarged as Figure 4.

improvement.justification: Additional diagnostics, disaggregated results, and the memory limitation improve documentation. However, v5 damages the central mathematical justification: v4's transformation connects Eqs. (4), (8), and (9) consistently, whereas v5 asserts Z = T† while retaining off-diagonal scaling in Eq. (9) that no longer follows from Eq. (4). Appendix A.3 also assumes a different operator from the new definition. These inconsistencies undermine the essential claim that the computed weights represent commute times, outweighing the reporting gains.
